swf_dust_axle.description: There's a broken axle out past the far turn of the Mirage Raceway, worth more than anything else left on the course. It's been there two seasons, and neither I nor the Dustwheel has taken it, though either of us could have, any day, without being seen. Go and look at it, and don't bring it back, because I'm not asking you to. Put the scrappers off it while you're there and bring me their tags. If they've tagged it, it's theirs by their rule, and I want to know that for certain instead of suspecting it for another two years.
swf_dust_axle.accept_text: You'll know it when you see it. It's the only thing out there that hasn't been stripped.
swf_dust_axle.turn_in_text:
They haven't tagged it.

Two seasons and nobody has claimed it, theirs or mine, and now I've got to decide what that means.

It means we both think the other one is going to need it more. That's a stupid thing for two businesses to think about each other, and I've been thinking it since the wet.

Take this to Winnow, who keeps the book. Tell her I sent you and don't tell her why.

swf_dust_cousins.description: Nobody in Saltwheel calls the Dustwheel bandits. Pim has you putting them off the course, and she's right to, but I want you to understand what you're doing, because she won't tell you. Half of them are somebody's cousin. When the track died, some of us walked into town and some of us walked out onto the pan, and mostly it came down to which way you were facing that week. Put off the boiler crews and bring me plates off them, and then come back and ask me what we call them.
swf_dust_cousins.accept_text: I want to be asked out loud. Don't let me off it.
swf_dust_cousins.turn_in_text:
There's the same fault in every plate, and it's our fault. They learned it from us, and we learned it from nobody. We worked it out, badly, over eleven years, and then taught it to the people we're now paying somebody to put off a road.

We don't call them anything. That's the answer, and you made me say it.

swf_dust_fuel.description: I laid in enough fuel to run a full season the year before the track died, and I've been sitting on it since. Before the sky changed I had two hundred racers on this pan, and now I've got six customers. The same season, the mountain turned up in the north, which I'm told is a coincidence, by people who aren't selling fuel. The wheelmen are burning something out there that isn't coming from me. Go after them and bring me their wheels, so I can see what it's doing to the rubber.
swf_dust_fuel.accept_text: I've done the arithmetic on who's at fault. I'll do it at you when you get back.
swf_dust_fuel.turn_in_text:
They're running it dry and lean and getting away with it, which means they've found something cheaper than what I sell.

So that's the rest of my customers gone, in front of me, with a wheel in my hand.

You came through same as the rest of them, and I'm not going to pretend I'm delighted. But you did the job, and this is what the job pays.

swf_dust_ledger.description: I record every cart in and out and every barrel of salt, written down twice. The town is shrinking and I can tell you by exactly how much, which makes me the least popular person in it. Pim sent you and didn't say why, which means she's finally worked it out and can't stand to be the one who says it. Bring me the Dustwheel crews' salvage tags and their pry bars, and put them on this bench. Then ask me what column they go in, the actual question, and I'll give you the actual answer.
swf_dust_ledger.accept_text: Nobody in this town has wanted the actual answer since the track died. Ask me anyway.
swf_dust_ledger.turn_in_text:
They go in as customers.

They've been buying fuel off somebody, parts off somebody, and salt off Jixa under a different name since the second winter. It's in this book, and it's been in this book the whole time.

The town is down by a figure I could say out loud. It's not down by as much as it thinks, and the difference is sitting out on that pan calling itself something else.

I'm going to put this in front of Tozzik, and he's going to have to decide whether they can enter.

swf_dust_rights.description: I own everything out on that track the day it stops moving. The rule's written down, it's older than the track, and it's made me the richest wreck-picker on a pan with no wrecks left on it. Read it and you'll find it says stopped, not slowed, not parked, and not abandoned by a crew that went into town for a season. The Dustwheel scrappers have been taking things that haven't stopped moving yet. Clear them off my course and bring me their pry bars.
swf_dust_rights.accept_text: Yes, it's a lot of effort for a rule nobody enforces. That's what a rule nobody enforces costs.
swf_dust_rights.turn_in_text:
Every one of these bars is flattened at the business end, because they've been using them as levers on things that were never meant to come apart.

I'd have taught them that in a morning. Nobody asked me to teach anybody anything.

Grizzik wants a word with you, and she won't enjoy having it.

swf_in_glass_pan.description: I can tell you whether a thing came up out of the mesas or down off the mountain. The shard the salt crew brought me did neither. It's pan fused to glass, and the only pan big enough to do that to itself is four days east of anywhere I've been. I've been pricing things off that pan for eleven years on the word of carters who never got out of the cart. Head east, past the last mesa, through the gap and out onto the white, and stand where it came from.
swf_in_glass_pan.accept_text: I don't need you to bring me anything. The birds will be a problem, though, so bring me their quills.
swf_in_glass_pan.turn_in_text:
There's a town out there?

Goblins, on a racetrack, on the edge of a salt flat that's eating them, and not one of the carters thought to mention it, because not one of them ever walked past their own cart.

I've spent eleven years treating that pan as weather. Go back out there and find out what they call it.

swf_in_other_end.description: Four caravans a week come up that ramp, not one of them on time, and every one of them comes from the north. Namka has a road with somebody at both ends of it now, and I've noticed there's a third end that nobody in Freewind Post has ever walked. Nothing's come from the east in my working life, and there's supposed to be a town out there. Walk to it, and put this in the hand of whoever keeps their books. Every town has one, and they're always the person nobody talks to.
swf_in_other_end.accept_text: Kill the Dustwheel scrappers you meet on that road. If I'm sending carts, I want to know what's on it.
swf_in_other_end.turn_in_text:
Winnow reads it twice, which is what she does with everything.

Freewind Post wants to know whether there's anything here worth a cart, and there is. I can tell him to the barrel what there is, and I've been able to for three years. This is the first time in those three years that anybody outside this town has asked me a question.

I'm going to answer it at a length he'll regret. Stay where you are, because you're carrying it back, and you may as well know what this place is while I write.

swf_inn_hinges.description: I can slow salt, but I can't stop it, and anyone who says otherwise is selling you grease. The inn's shutters haven't latched in a year, and Vozzi's stopped mentioning it. Here's a thing the hives are better at than we are, which I resent and which is true. Sentinel plate has salt grown right through it and still articulates, and ours seizes in a season. Bring me sentinel plates and the wet resin, and let me find out whether it's the plate or what they bed it in.
swf_inn_hinges.accept_text: It's for a shutter. I'm aware of the scale of the ambition.
swf_inn_hinges.turn_in_text:
It's the resin, and the plate is ordinary. They bed every joint in something that never fully sets, so the salt gets in and gets pushed back out every time the joint moves.

That's a hinge that cleans itself by being used. Three years it's been walking past my shop on eight legs.

The shutter at the end latches now. Don't tell her it was me, or she'll want the other eleven done and I've got a trade to run.

swf_inn_no_bird.description: There's a post outside this inn of exactly the kind a wind rider perches on, and there's never been a wind rider on it. I've explained that to every arrival for eleven years, so before you ask, there was never a wind rider, you came in on your feet, and that's how you're leaving. Bed, board and a bind, that's the full list. What I've got is a flock of salt vultures roosting on the post, because it's the tallest thing in town and they aren't fussy about what it was for. Kill those and bring me quills, and then I'll hear no more about birds from anybody.
swf_inn_no_bird.accept_text: Your bed's the one at the end, when you're done.
swf_inn_no_bird.turn_in_text:
That's them off the post and off my roof.

I've had that post taken down twice and put back up twice, by different people, for different reasons, and neither of them could tell me what the reason was.

It stays up, and I've stopped asking myself why. Your bed is the one at the end, and the shutter doesn't latch.

swf_inn_stock.description: I laid in years of stock the year before the track died, for a crowd that was coming and then didn't. It's all still in the warehouse, in good order, because I've kept it that way, and you can decide whether that's professional or sad. The Dustwheel have been into the back of the warehouse twice this season, and I'd rather deal with it than report it. Reporting it means Winnow writes it down, and once Winnow writes something down it's a fact about this town forever. Put off the boiler crews and bring me their plates and pry bars.
swf_inn_stock.accept_text: That's what they left behind. I want it accounted for.
swf_inn_stock.turn_in_text:
That's accounted for, and I'm going to tell you something I haven't told Winnow.

They didn't take anything the second time. They put something back, a crate of plate in our pattern, better made than ours.

So either somebody's out there paying a debt nobody recorded, or they're being polite, and I've got no column for either.

Take what you're owed. The stock was never going to move, and at least it's moving now.

swf_inn_two_years.description: Vozzi runs the beds and I run the bar, and we haven't exchanged a word in two years. The business has never been better, and we've both noticed, which is the problem. She needs scourers for the pots, and she won't ask me for them, and I'm not offering. So you're going to bring me mandibles and put them behind this bar, where she'll see them when she comes through for the ice. She'll take them, she won't say anything, and that'll be that.
swf_inn_two_years.accept_text: Then ask me what we fell out about. Everyone does eventually.
swf_inn_two_years.turn_in_text:
You want to know what it was.

I don't remember. I've thought about it properly, more than once, in the quiet hours, and it's gone.

I'm certain she remembers. That means one of us is carrying it and it isn't me, and after two years asking her would be the cruellest thing in this building.

She took the mandibles, I watched her take them. Go on, get out of my bar.

swf_item_entry_slip.description: You turn the slip over. It's an entry for the Saltwheel Open, three seasons out of date, with the name scratched out and written in again twice. It's the same hand each time, pressing harder every go. Somebody entered, withdrew, entered, withdrew, and entered again, and then the race never happened. The gantry is where entries are taken, and the man under it takes them whether or not anybody brings him one.
swf_item_entry_slip.accept_text: Watch for the wheelmen on your way in. They won't step aside for somebody carrying paper.
swf_item_entry_slip.turn_in_text:
Tozzik reads it, and reads it again, and doesn't look up.

That's his hand. He entered the year it died and pulled out, and entered, and pulled out, and entered.

I never processed the third one. It came in after the date and I'm a man who keeps the date, so I put it in a drawer and said nothing, and he's spent three winters believing nobody wanted him on the line.

Nazzik is in the inn. I'm not going over there tonight. I'll go tomorrow, and I'm not saying that to get out of it.

swf_item_sealed_tin.description: You turn the tin over. It's lead-sealed at every seam, and it was dug up out of pan that's been bone dry for longer than anyone has been counting. Something rattles inside, and whatever's in there has never once been wet. The tunnelers bring these up and leave them, which means there are more, and somebody was sealing things in lead on this pan before anybody in Saltwheel was born. Go back to where the spoil comes up on the Brine, then put the tin in front of the only person in town who seals things in lead.
swf_item_sealed_tin.accept_text: Bring loads of the spoil with you. Brewer Nissa Tolk will want to see what it came out of.
swf_item_sealed_tin.turn_in_text:
Nissa holds it up to the lamp and turns it slowly, and she doesn't open it.

That's my seam. It isn't my work, but it's my seam, the double fold. My mother taught me it, her people brought it here from somewhere else entirely, and I've never seen it on anything I didn't make.

It came up out of ground that's been dry for a very long time.

I'm not opening it in front of you, and I'm not opening it tonight. Come back in the spring and I'll tell you what my family was doing under this pan before there was a town on it.

swf_mound_five.description: I can see five mounds from the east fence. Three years ago there were two, and the near one was twice as far out. I say the number in the inn every evening, and they've started buying me drinks so that I say it quieter. The skitterers come off the near one and work west along the fence line. Clear a dozen of them off and bring me mandibles, and look at the salt on them when you take them, because it grows over the edge and doesn't blunt it.
swf_mound_five.accept_text: I want to know if that's true of all of them, or just the ones I've seen.
swf_mound_five.turn_in_text:
It's true of all of them.

So it can't be damage or age. That's how they're made, and a thing that's made that way on a salt pan didn't end up here by accident.

They belong here now. That's a worse sentence than the number is.

swf_mound_mouths.description: There are two ways down into the Undercrust, and they're most of the pan apart. The Crustfall is a shallow slot by Crustbreak, and the Deep Shaft is out under the oldest mound on the map. I've assumed since I took this post that they're two caves. Go to the Crustfall first, then all the way across to the Deep Shaft, and kill the tunnelers in between. Stand at both and tell me whether the air coming out of them smells the same.
swf_mound_mouths.accept_text: I'm not asking you to go in. If it smells the same, I've been counting two caves for four winters.
swf_mound_mouths.turn_in_text:
It smells the same at both, so it's one hole.

Most of this pan is standing on one hole with two mouths, and I've been writing two numbers in two columns since the first winter like a man who can't add up.

I'm going to go and say that in the inn tonight at full volume, and they can buy me whatever they like.

swf_mound_moved.description: The mound I call the near one isn't where it was at the start of the wet. Mounds don't move, and I've checked my own sightings four times, off the same two fence posts I've always used. Go out to the First Mound and stand at the foot of it, because I need somebody who hasn't been staring at it every evening to tell me what shape it is. Kill the crawlers while you're there and bring me their resin. If they're laying fresh on the west face and the east face is old, it didn't move, it grew toward the fence.
swf_mound_moved.accept_text: That's a different problem, with a different arithmetic attached. Bring me the resin.
swf_mound_moved.turn_in_text:
Fresh on the west and old on the east, so it grew.

It grew toward us, at a rate I can now calculate, and I'm going to calculate it tonight. Then I'll have to decide whether to say the new number in the inn.

They'll buy me drinks either way. That's what I've learned about this town.

swf_mound_queen.description: One cave, two mouths, and at the heart of it something that's been laying since before anybody in Saltwheel was born. I've stopped counting mounds, because there's no point counting the branches when you've found the root. Go in at whichever mouth you like, they both get there, and the Undercrust is a long way south of town, under the far edge of the pan. Kill the rippers on the way and bring me plates off the sentinels, because I want to see whether what guards her is made the same as what comes out to the fence. I'm not coming, because my one skill is counting, and down there there's nothing to count.
swf_mound_queen.accept_text: She's at the middle. You'll know her when the tunnels stop.
swf_mound_queen.turn_in_text:
They're made exactly the same, root to branch, and she was the root.

It doesn't end it. You know that and I know that. There are four more mounds out there and a hole under all of them.

But the near one has stopped growing west this week, measured off the same two posts. It's the first time the number has gone the other way since I took this post, and I'm going to enjoy it for exactly one evening.

swf_mound_salt.description: I seal everything in lead because salt air takes a cork in a season. I've been reading Brak's notes over his shoulder in the inn, and I've noticed something he hasn't, because I think about salt as a substance and not a price. Brak counts the mounds, and nobody asks what's coming out of them. The tunnelers bring spoil up and leave it, so bring me loads of it, and more mandibles to set against it. The pan is salt all the way down, and if what they're bringing up is dry, we've got a problem nobody in this town is equipped to think about.
swf_mound_salt.accept_text: Bring it in a sealed sack if you can. I want to know how dry it is, not how dry the walk made it.
swf_mound_salt.turn_in_text:
It's bone dry, all of it, from under a pan that should be wet through at that depth.

So they're digging through what's under the salt, and what's under it has no water in it any more. I'd very much like to know when it stopped having water in it.

Somebody has asked this question before, and it wasn't anybody here. Go and find out where.

swf_mound_spitters.description: I treat salt sores, sun, and whatever the bugs do to a hand, in that order, every season. The third one's been climbing for two years, and I've stopped pretending it hasn't. A spitter gets resin into a wound and the wound sets, with the dirt still in it, and then I'm cutting it open again in a fortnight. Clear the hive spitters off the fence line along the Mounds, east of Saltwheel. Bring me sacs still under pressure, and scorpid barbs to set against them, because the barbs keep their venom wet out here when everything else dries.
swf_mound_spitters.accept_text: It's crude medicine, but it's the medicine available.
swf_mound_spitters.turn_in_text:
They're all still under pressure, which is what I needed.

The barb keeps wet because of something in the sheath, and the resin sets because of something it's missing. Between the two of them I've got an afternoon's work and possibly a hand saved in the spring.

That's the best sentence I've said in this surgery in a year.

swf_open_course.description: The Mirage Raceway is a loop out across the northern pan and back to the straight. It was surveyed once, eleven years ago, and nobody's walked it since the hives came up, so I've been posting a course I haven't seen. Go out to the far turn and look at it, which is more than I've done. The glasswing darters have taken the north leg, and they come off the ground fast enough to put a driver into the salt, so clear them. Bring me resin too, from the drones that lay it on the Crust, south-west of town, because I need to know whether the course is fouled or whether something's building on it.
swf_open_course.accept_text: Whichever one it turns out to be decides whether there's a race.
swf_open_course.turn_in_text:
Something's building on it. That resin is structural, so they aren't just crossing my course. They're putting something down on it, and the far turn is inside whatever they're putting down.

So the loop is gone, and the straight isn't. A race on the straight alone isn't an Open and I'm going to call it one anyway, and you're the only person who'll ever know that I know.

swf_open_date.description: I post the times for the Saltwheel Open on the first clear day after the winter wet, with entries at the gantry, scrutineering at noon, and the flag at two. Nobody's entered for three seasons, and I post them anyway, in a clean hand, and stand under the board for an hour in case somebody comes. The start line wants clearing before anything else happens. The Dustwheel scrappers have been stripping the kerb markers since the wet, and every marker they take is a yard of the line I can't certify. Clear them off the straight and bring me the salvage tags they hang on whatever they strip.
swf_open_date.accept_text: The tags are numbered. I want to know which markers I've lost, not just how many.
swf_open_date.turn_in_text:
They're numbered in order, which means one person pulled them in one afternoon and didn't hurry.

I'm not angry about the markers. I'm angry that it took me until the tags to work out nobody had been out to look.

Right, then, scrutineering is at noon and I've got no scrutineer.

swf_open_entries.description: The board's up, the scrutineer's ready, and the entry column has been blank for three seasons. I won't ask anyone directly, because asking would make it a favour, and a favour doesn't count as an entry. You aren't from here and it costs you nothing, so you can ask for me. Nazzik holds the course record and will tell you so, Grizzik keeps a crew for a race that doesn't run and pays half of it herself, and Mozz has fuel and no one to sell it to. Ask all three, and don't persuade anybody, because I want to know what they say when nobody's leaning on them.
swf_open_entries.accept_text: Ask me about them first if you need to. Then go and ask them, and lean on nobody.
swf_open_entries.turn_in_text:
So that's one record-holder who won't drive, one pit boss who'd crew it tomorrow, and Mozz.

Mozz said he'd supply the fuel at cost on condition somebody tells the newcomers this is their fault. I'm not putting that on a board.

But he said he'd supply it. Write that down and leave the rest.

swf_open_flagfall.description: I've got a crew of hands on the payroll for a race that hasn't run since the wet before last, and Tozzik pays half and I pay half. Here's the part nobody says in front of him. The Dustwheel know the date too, they've been running the straight themselves since the wet, and they'll be on it at two whether we are or not. So the straight gets cleared properly this time, wheelmen and boiler crews both. Bring the wheels back, the flat-spotted ones off machines that were actually driven, because I want to see what they've been doing with my course.
swf_open_flagfall.accept_text: Flat spots tell you how a wheel was driven. Get me the ones with the worst of them.
swf_open_flagfall.turn_in_text:
Every one is flat-spotted on one side. They've been locking the wheels at the same mark on every run, which means they're racing each other out there, properly, and timing it.

Three years I've been paying half a crew to sit in a shed, and the sport never stopped. It just stopped being ours.

Go and tell Tozzik the flag drops at two.

swf_open_record.description: The flag dropped at two, and there was one entrant, on the straight alone, because the loop belongs to something else now. I timed it myself, because the only other person who knows how was driving. Before I post it, I want something done by somebody who wasn't here for the good years. Walk the straight, end to end, at the pace a person walks. Then put the mound sentinels off the eastern mark and bring me plates off them, because that's where the course used to turn, and I want to know what's standing on it now.
swf_open_record.accept_text: I'll post the time either way. I'd rather post it knowing.
swf_open_record.turn_in_text:
It's worse than the record by a margin I'm not going to say out loud, on a course a third the size of the one the record was set on.

I've posted it anyway.

Nazzik will tell you his record stands, and he's right. He won't tell you he was under the board at six this morning reading the new time. I saw him, and he saw me see him.

The date held. That's what I had, and I held it.

swf_open_scrutineer.description: I've scrutineered every Open since I was old enough to hold the gauge, and nobody's asked me since the track died. I said yes before Tozzik finished the sentence, which embarrassed us both. If anything runs on that straight, it runs on a boiler, and I won't pass a boiler I haven't seen plate from. Bring me pieces off the Dustwheel crews, because they're running the same pattern we did and running it badly, which makes their failures useful to me. Bring me pry bars too, and those aren't for the race, they're for me.
swf_open_scrutineer.accept_text: Somebody once drove that straight with no boiler at all. I've taken one apart since, and I wish I hadn't.
swf_open_scrutineer.turn_in_text:
Every one of them is blued in a ring. It's the same fault we had and never fixed, and they haven't fixed it either.

There's a comfort in that I'm not proud of.

Tell Tozzik his scrutineer is ready. Tell him I said it like it was nothing.

swf_salt_back.description: I run four caravans a week up the ramp and not one of them on time. Ovi wants a cart on the Saltwheel pan, and I've told her no every season because of what's on the road, and I don't mean the hives, I mean the crews. Clear the Dustwheel scrappers off the west crossing and bring me their salvage tags. If the tags are numbered in sequence, it's one outfit working a route, and I can negotiate with an outfit, but if they're scattered, it's nobody, and I can't. Take Ovi's reply back down to Jixa Brinecount with you as well.
swf_salt_back.accept_text: Ovi wrote it standing up, which from her is a great deal.
swf_salt_back.turn_in_text:
They're in sequence, so it's one outfit and one route, with a schedule I can read off a handful of tin tags.

I can work with that. I've worked with worse, and I married one of them.

Tell Brinecount the cart comes in the spring, and tell her I said if, in the voice I use for if. She'll know it. Everyone who ships out of a dying town knows that voice.

swf_salt_cart.description: I sell what a person needs to walk out of Saltwheel, and business is thriving, because walking out is the only option available. Jixa wants her salt in Freewind Post, and there's no cart, no bird and no road worth the word, but there's you. The west crossing goes past the Brine, and the mirage basilisks have the Brine. Kill them and bring me eyes, which I sell to people who think they're lucky, and before you ask, they aren't. Bring me scorpid barbs as well, because those actually work for what I say they do.
swf_salt_cart.accept_text: There's no bird. I'll mention it again later, too.
swf_salt_cart.turn_in_text:
These are clouded right through. Looking into one is like looking down the pan at noon, which is exactly what I tell the buyers and exactly why they buy them.

The crossing is open. Go and tell Jixa, and then come back to me, because she's going to send you across it and you'll want the kit, and I'm going to sell it to you.

There's no bird. I've mentioned that, and I'll mention it again.

swf_salt_crossing.description: Freewind Post sits over a long drop at the far end of the mesas, and between it and Saltwheel there's a pan, a range, and nothing that flies for hire. I've been shipping to Spice-Trader Ovi there for eleven years, and we've never met. She's never once haggled, which told me everything I needed to know about her and nothing about what she looks like. These are the sacks, graded and sealed. When you get up there, ask her the question I've never been able to put in a letter.
swf_salt_crossing.accept_text: She'll know which question. If she doesn't, she isn't the woman I've been trading with.
swf_salt_crossing.turn_in_text:
Ovi turns one of the sacks so the seal faces her, and she doesn't open it.

Eleven years, and she wants to know whether I still think it's boring.

Tell her yes. Tell her I've got three climates on one table now, and the only thing on it that's never caused me a day's trouble is her salt. The mountain can do what it likes as long as the pan keeps drying.

And tell her the caravans will come. Bohl has been saying it for a year, and one of these years he'll be right.

swf_salt_graded.description: Salt from the shore is clean and salt from the crust isn't, and the difference is money. I grade it myself, by eye, with a vulture quill, and I've never once been wrong in a way the buyer noticed. Go out onto the Crust and bring me what the tunnelers have thrown up, because it's the deepest salt anybody can get at without digging, and I've believed for twenty years the deepest is the cleanest. Put the crustback scorpids off the drying ground while you're out there. They get into the stacks, and then somebody finds one in a barrel in Freewind Post and I hear about it for a year.
swf_salt_graded.accept_text: I've believed that about deep salt on no evidence at all. Bring me some evidence.
swf_salt_graded.turn_in_text:
That's the cleanest I've graded. Twenty years of guessing and it turns out I was right, which is worth less than being able to prove it, but it's worth something.

Now for the problem.

I've got the best salt I've ever had and no way to get it anywhere, because the cart doesn't come any more.

swf_salt_one_trade.description: I deal in salt, that's the whole business, and everybody laughed at me for twenty years for it. Nobody's laughing now, and most of them are just gone. Salt's the only trade on this pan the Integration didn't touch, because nothing that came through needed a racetrack, and everything that came through needs to eat. The salt vultures are at the drying racks on the shore, and they've worked out that a rack is a table. Kill them and bring me quills, because I use them for marking grades.
swf_salt_one_trade.accept_text: I'd buy the quills off you anyway. Bring every one you find.
swf_salt_one_trade.turn_in_text:
Every one is salt-stiff, which is what makes them good for grading. They don't bend, so they don't lie about the line they drew.

You'll have heard a lot of complaining in this town and most of that's fair. Mine is the one ledger that went up, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise just to be sociable.

swf_solo_crew.description: My crew haven't touched a running machine since the track died, and two of them have started forgetting things you can't relearn off a book. So I'm sending you out to bring me work. Go after the Dustwheel wheelmen and bring me their wheels and salvage tags, so I know which machine each wheel came off. My hands strip them, rebuild them and put them on a shelf, and then I pay them. I'm not doing it for a race, I'm doing it so their hands remember the work.
swf_solo_crew.accept_text: Bring me the worst wheels you find. The worse they are, the more my hands learn.
swf_solo_crew.turn_in_text:
They had all of them apart before I'd finished telling them what they were.

One of them cried about it, in the shed, where he thought I couldn't see. I let him, and then I handed him the second one.

That's my whole management philosophy, and it's never once failed me.

swf_solo_lead.description: Salt air ruins a cork in a season, so I seal everything in lead and charge you for the lead. I've heard what they say about lead, and I'd like you to drink it fast. The crustback scorpids keep their venom wet in air that dries everything else, because of something in the sheath. If I can get at what the sheath is doing, I can stop sealing in lead and stop charging you for it. Clear them off the drying ground and bring me their barbs.
swf_solo_lead.accept_text: I'd like to stop charging you for lead. I'd like that on the record.
swf_solo_lead.turn_in_text:
Whatever is in the sheath, it's built into it, not painted on.

That means I can't copy it with what I've got on this bench, and I'll be sealing in lead for another year at least.

Still, knowing I can't do a thing is worth something. It's worth less than doing it, but I'll take it.

swf_solo_prices.description: Everything on my table came across the pan on a cart with four bad wheels, so you'll think my prices are high, and they are. Yes, they were lower four years ago, and that's about when the sky rearranged itself and half my suppliers found more interesting customers. I'm not blaming you personally, I'm blaming the general situation, of which you're a part. The saltcrust skitterers have got into my stock yard. Get them out and bring me their mandibles.
swf_solo_prices.accept_text: They're in the sacks. They're always in the sacks.
swf_solo_prices.turn_in_text:
That's them out of the sacks, and I'll drop what I charge you by a bit, and not by as much as you're hoping.

I'm not blaming you personally. I'm blaming the general situation, of which you're a part, and saying that out loud to one person at a time is the only satisfaction available to me.

swf_solo_record.description: The course record for the Saltwheel Open is mine, and nobody's touched it in eleven years. That's because nobody's driven the course in three, I'm aware of that, and it doesn't take the record off me. There's a marker stone at the north turn of the Mirage Raceway with a time cut into it. I want to know whether it's still legible. I'm not going out to look, and I'm not going to explain why.
swf_solo_record.accept_text: The darters are all over that leg. Clear them while you're up there.
swf_solo_record.turn_in_text:
So you can still read it.

That's good, that's really good. I'll tell you the thing I don't say in the inn. A record only counts while people are trying to take it, and the day they stopped trying it turned into a number on a rock.

Tozzik posted a new time this week, worse than mine by a long way. It's the best morning I've had in a long time.

swf_solo_shrinking.description: Every cart in, every cart out, every barrel of salt, written down twice. I'm the least popular person in Saltwheel, because I'm the only one who can answer the question this town asks itself at night. I need tunnel spoil to weigh against last year's, and vulture quills to write with, because I've used mine up and the general goods has stopped stocking them. That last part's a data point, and I've recorded it. Then ask me the question, because everyone wants to and nobody does.
swf_solo_shrinking.accept_text: I'd like, once, to be asked instead of avoided.
swf_solo_shrinking.turn_in_text:
We're down by a quarter, over three years, in bodies. In trade it's worse, and I won't say the figure because it isn't mine to hand to a stranger.

People think I keep this book to be unpleasant. I keep it because when a place goes, it goes without anybody writing down what was in it, and I've decided that isn't happening here.

That's all of it. You asked, and nobody asks.

swf_water_answer.description: The melt is higher every spring on the mountain, nobody on the mesas can say where that water goes, and the pan it should arrive on is drier than its own waterline. Those three have never been in one room, and you've stood in all three, which nobody else this side of the range has done. I think the water arrives, and always has. I think something underneath has been drinking it for longer than this town has existed, and the mountain has started sending more. Go out to the Deep Pan, put off the mound sentinels round the oldest mound on it, and bring me their plates and spoil from its foot.
swf_water_answer.accept_text: Spoil from the very foot of it, mind. That's where I'll know if I'm right.
swf_water_answer.turn_in_text:
These are wet. Every load from the foot of the Deep Mound is damp, out of a pan that's bone dry four miles west of here.

So it arrives, and it's never stopped arriving. It goes under, and it goes east, and it ends up beneath the oldest hive on this pan. That hive has been sitting on the only wet ground in the flats since before the first goblin saw this place, and it's been getting more of it every spring since the range came down.

Nobody made that happen. A mountain arrived, the water it sheds found the lowest thing it could, and the lowest thing was already occupied.

I'm going to write this down and send a copy up the mesas, and in about forty years somebody will read all three parts together and understand this pan.

swf_water_three.description: The tunnelers bring up dry spoil from under a pan that should be wet through, and I've held that fact for a season, waiting for a second one. Now Oyla's brought me a waterline. So I've got two facts, the pan was deeper and the ground beneath the pan is dry, and they don't sit together without a third thing between them. Bring me more loads of spoil, from as far east as you're willing to walk, and basilisk eyes. The eyes cloud by taking up whatever's in the air, and I can read a dry season off one the way you read a ring off a tree.
swf_water_three.accept_text: I need a few eyes to argue with each other. One on its own tells me nothing.
swf_water_three.turn_in_text:
The eastern spoil is drier than the western, and the eyes agree with each other, and none of this is a Saltwheel-sized question any more.

Water comes off a mountain in the north. It crosses the mesas, and it should arrive here. Somebody on that mountain has been watching their melt get bigger every spring, and somebody on those mesas has been asking where it goes. If you've stood in front of either of them, you already know more than I do.

Come back when you have, and not before. I'd only be guessing, and I'm too old to guess in front of company.

swf_water_waterline.description: There are shore stacks out on the western pan, lumps of rock the salt hasn't finished eating, and every one of them carries a waterline. I noticed it with a gauge in my hand, looking for something else entirely. The stain's at the same height on all of them, which means it's a waterline and not a coincidence, and it's a long way above where any water's been in my lifetime. Go out to the stacks on the west shore and mark it for me, because a vulture quill takes a mark on wet rock and holds it. Put the drones off the stacks while you're at it.
swf_water_waterline.accept_text: They're working the base of the stacks. I don't want my marks eaten.
swf_water_waterline.turn_in_text:
It's the same height on all of them, to within a hand.

This pan was deeper than this. I don't mean in a story or a song. I mean measurably, at a height I can put a gauge on, and recently enough that the stain hasn't gone.

So where did it go? I'm really asking. I want the answer, and I don't have the range to go and get it.
